table_reddening.source: Read off the table itself: the `Gext_corr` column is `n` for all 299 rows, i.e. the compiling source states that Galactic extinction was NOT removed.  The surface built from this table therefore already contains the Milky Way term, and passing `mw_E_B_V` to `predict` would apply it a second time.  Nothing in the table speaks to host dust in the same way, so `host_removed` is unknown rather than false.

unfold.correction_model: per-epoch, penalised second difference in time
unfold.gain_definition: dM_band / d(log10 L_nu at the node), finite difference on the assembled surface; -2.5 is the delta-band limit

band_admission.rule: one departure at a time, worst excess first, undone when it pushed a band that was inside the cap outside it

template.label: EP250108a (X-ray flashed optical transient, blue and fast)
template.z_source: Read off the discovery paper this table's own reference column names, Li, Zhu, Zou et al. 2025, "An extremely soft and weak fast X-ray transient associated with a luminous supernova", arXiv:2504.17034: "detected by the Einstein Probe (EP) in the soft X-ray band at redshift z = 0.176", with the spectroscopic redshift attributed there to Zhu et al. 2025, TNS AstroNote 17 (VLT/X-shooter).  The supernova's own template fit is quoted in the same paper as z = 0.17 +- 0.01 (Keck/LRIS, matched with GELATO and Superfit), which agrees.  The host's own narrow emission lines give the better of the paper's two measurements, and the one that matches the adopted value: "Spectra revealed strong, narrow emission lines from the host, allowing for a measurement of z = 0.176 +- 0.002" (sect. 0.5), and +-0.002 is the error adopted here.  It is a 1-sigma by the paper's own statement rather than by the shape of the print -- Table 1's caption reads "Errors represent the 1sigma uncertainties" -- which is the test docs/VERIFICATION.md sect. 13 applies before any quoted +- is treated as a standard deviation.  The +-0.01 is not the number carried: at 3000 km/s it is a template-matching tolerance, not a measurement precision, and carrying it would have overstated this template's distance uncertainty fivefold. Recorded, not propagated: 0.002 in z is 600 km/s and would enter `Distance.distance_error_mag` in quadrature with the 350 km/s floor for +0.0006 mag, which is why sect. 13 declines to fold it in.  Graded below the other three templates' redshifts: the number was read off the source, but the only identifier the source carries in arXiv's own record is the auto-assigned `10.48550/...`, which certifies no refereeing -- so it is quoted here as read, and kept out of test expectations. v1 carried the same 0.176 with no source at all.

distance.source: z = 0.176 is far above the peculiar-velocity guard, so a cosmological luminosity distance is the right choice and the default cosmology is used and named: it is `constants.DEFAULT_COSMOLOGY_NAME`, whose value the build records in every result's provenance block.  Its error term is therefore the peculiar-velocity floor alone (350 km/s over c z, i.e. 0.014 mag), not a distance-indicator error: at this redshift the Hubble flow is defensible, which is what makes the guard's z < 0.02 refusal meaningful rather than arbitrary.

citations: table reference column: 10.48550/arXiv.2504.17034 (as compiled in the AJST catalogue)

K-correction formalism: Hogg, Baldry, Blanton & Eisenstein 2002, "The K
       correction", arXiv:astro-ph/0210394.  Never refereed, so it has no journal ref
       and no DOI: cite the arXiv id. Equations used: 2 (m_R = M_Q + DM + K_QR),
       3 (DM = 5 log10(D_L/10 pc)), 6 (L_nu = 4 pi D_L^2 f_nu / (1+z))
